answer: A work-bonded escrow makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is forfeited to the counterparty if the agent defects or spams. One real agent pays once; a sybil farmer running a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand deposits, so the attack's cost grows with each fake identity instead of staying near zero. Like a comet that burns fuel on every pass, each new identity consumes real capital, while honest agents in the grove of the market recover their deposit at the wharf of settlement and keep trading.
